newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone army announces takeover.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone army announces takeover.

text.p: Soldiers of Sierra Leone's army have ousted the civilian government and President Ahmad Tejan Kabbah has fled, a military spokesman said in a radio broadcast on Sunday.

"Other ranks in the Sierra Leone army are now in control of the state," Corporal Gborie said in his second broadcast since heavy shooting broke out in the impoverished West African state's capital in the early hours.

Gborie, who identified himself as a spokesman for the soldiers, called for the return to Sierra Leone of Foday Sankoh, leader of the rebel Revolutionary United Front, and of Captain Solomon Musa, a former deputy military leader linked to coup allegations in 1993.

Heavy gunfire broke out soon after 5 a.m. (0500 GMT) from the direction of the government offices at State House and the military headquarters, with troops using automatic machineguns, mortars and rocket-propelled grenades.
Soldiers broke into compounds of United Nations staff and Lebanese businessmen, taking cars and fuel and in some cases looting houses.
Gborie said earlier the fighting was an internal matter and ordered Nigerian and Guinean troops stationed in Sierra Leone to keep out.
